content.title: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe

content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Gumroad payhip

Gumroad and Payhip promise simplicity: upload a product, set a price, and sell. But this simplicity comes with dependencies. Both rely on Stripe or PayPal for payments, which excludes creators in restricted countries. They also host your files and manage delivery, meaning you’re renting their infrastructure. In contrast, sovereign commerce infrastructure gives you ownership. GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages host your store for free. Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script handle backend logic. Supabase or Google Sheets store orders. Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 delivers files. NOWPayments processes crypto payments with a 0.5% fee and no KYC. The Edge Commerce Stack integrates these tools into a unified system. It’s not just a store—it’s a fully operational commerce stack you own. No platform can shut you down, and no country restriction applies. The tradeoff? You manage deployment. But the result is infrastructure sovereignty, not platform dependency.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Gumroad and Payhip are clear: if Stripe or PayPal isn’t available in your country, you can’t sell. They’re built on top of these payment processors, inheriting their restrictions. This isn’t a flaw—it’s their architecture. Sovereign commerce infrastructure avoids this entirely. It uses NOWPayments to accept 300+ cryptocurrencies, bypassing traditional financial systems. Recommended networks like BSC, Solana, and TRON keep transaction fees under $0.10. This isn’t a workaround—it’s a structural alternative. The Edge Commerce Stack deploys this in 48 hours, configured for your products and tested end-to-end. It’s designed for regions where conventional platforms fail. You’re not working around restrictions—you’re operating outside their scope. This is infrastructure built for permanence, not temporary access.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Gumroad and Payhip charge 10% and 5% per sale, respectively, on top of Stripe’s 2.9% + $0.30. In restricted countries, these fees are irrelevant—you can’t use them. Crypto payments via NOWPayments charge 0.5% with no monthly fees or hidden costs. Payments confirm on-chain instantly, triggering automatic delivery. The Edge Commerce Stack includes this integration, ensuring you keep 99.5% of every sale. There’s no platform fee, no subscription, and no revenue share. The $197 deployment cost is a one-time expense. Compare this to renting a platform indefinitely. The real cost of Gumroad or Payhip isn’t their fee—it’s the inability to sell at all. Sovereign infrastructure eliminates both the fee and the restriction.
Sovereign infrastructure replaces platforms you can’t use.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

With Gumroad and Payhip, your store, files, and customer data live on their servers. They control access, and you’re subject to their terms. Sovereign infrastructure inverts this. Your store is hosted on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. Your files are stored in Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Orders are logged in Supabase or Google Sheets. You own every component. The Edge Commerce Stack automates this entire process. Once payment confirms, the system delivers the product instantly. No manual intervention. No platform dependency. After deployment, COREMERCH has no access—you own the stack entirely. This is infrastructure sovereignty. It’s not just about selling—it’s about owning the means of commerce.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If you’re in a country where Stripe and PayPal operate, Gumroad or Payhip might suffice. But if you’re in Nigeria, Ghana, or Zimbabwe, these platforms are non-starters. Sovereign commerce infrastructure is the only structural alternative. It’s built for creators in regions where conventional systems fail. The Edge Commerce Stack is deployed in 48 hours, configured for your products, and tested end-to-end. It’s not a temporary solution—it’s a permanent shift to infrastructure ownership. If you’re selling digital products and need control, scalability, and permanence, this is your architecture. It’s not the easiest path, but it’s the only one that ensures you’re never locked out again.

Verify SPF/DKIM/DMARC for email deliverability. 9. Monitor transactions via webhook notifications. 10. Scale as needed—you own the entire infrastructure.
